newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES, CARDINALS CLOSE IN ON DIVISION TITLES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES, CARDINALS CLOSE IN ON DIVISION TITLES.

text.p: The Atlanta Braves and the St Louis Cardinals on Thursday moved to just one game each of winning their National League divisional playoffs.

The Braves beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 3-2 with three solo home runs and a masterful pitching performance by Greg Maddox, who limited the slumping Dodger hitters to just two unearned runs and three hits in seven innings.
Los Angeles has managed just eight runs in its last six games and is batting .123 (8-for-65) in the first two games of this series. Braves' pitchers have a 0.47 ERA in the series.
Maddux, who has won the last four National League Cy Young Awards as the its best pitcher, threw 72 pitches. Only 14 were balls.
The three Braves' homers were hit by Fred McGriff and rookie Jermaine Dye in the top of the seventh inning and Ryan Klesko in the second inning.

"Yesterday I was 0 for 4," Dye said. "I decided I had to stay relaxed .... It's a dream to come up in my first year and play on a championship team and win the game with a home run." I tried to get a fast ball but they hung a curve on me."
In St Louis, the Cardinals beat the San Diego Padres 5-4 also to move within one victory of winning their best-of-five-games series.
Tom Pagnozzi's eighth-inning grounder off pitcher Trevor Hoffman's glove scored Brian Jordan with the leading run for St Louis.
Rick Honeycutt (1-0) pitched a scoreless eighth for the win before Dennis Eckersley recorded his second save in as many games with a nine-pitch ninth. It was Eckersley's 13th career post-season save.
San Diego rallied from a 4-1 deficit with two runs in the sixth and one in the eighth.

Ken Caminiti, who had failed to put the ball in play in his first five at-bats in the series with four strikeouts and a walk, led off the fifth inning for the Padres with a 392-foot blast over the right-field wall to tie the game.

But the Cardinals struck back for three runs in their half of the fifth. Cardinals' starting pitcher Andy Benes had a one-out single and Smith followed with a single. Willie McGee walked to load the bases, chasing Sanders for Dario Veras. Five pitches later, Ron Gant belted a 2-2 pitch over the head of Finley in centre, clearing the bases for a 4-1 St. Louis lead.
Gant said Brian Jordan, who was on deck, "told me just swing straight and swing hard."
After fouling off the first pitch Gant "took an easier swing on the hit and drove the ball over his head. You've got to hit the ball pretty hard to get it over Finley's head."
Padres' manager Bruce Bochy said: "We made a mistake on that. Steve Finley is a gold glove outfielder and something went wrong there."

Benes, a former Padre, retired the first 12 batters he faced, striking out six, before Caminiti hit his first career post-season homer. Benes allowed four runs and six hits in seven-plus innings with a walk and nine strikeouts.
The big hitters of the San Diego lineup -- Finley, Caminiti and Wally Joyner -- are a combined 3-for-20 in the series with one RBI. The Padres are 2-for-12 with runners in scoring position.
